inference.step: The day (1 July) is the day of the whole account; A history of 1913 puts Lee on Seminary Ridge about half-past four 'just as the Federal troops were retreating'; Long (1876) says Lee arrived 'near the close of the battle' and Taylor (1877) that Lee watched the flight through the town. All three put Lee's sight of the retreat late in the day; none gives a clock, and the 1913 book's own source is not named.

reason_not_chosen.text: It dates Lee reaching Seminary Ridge at the end of the fight, a later stage than reaching the field. The book of 1913 names no source and Pendleton, who was with Lee, puts him on the field about two hours earlier.

weighing.summary: The plan lists 13:30 and 14:30, both from web pages that could not be read, and no source found gives either. The one witness who gives an hour is General Pendleton, Lee's chief of artillery, who rode with him from Cashtown: when they took position overlooking the field it was 'perhaps, 2 o'clock' (report of 12 Sep 1863). Early (1878) repeats 'about two' from Pendleton and Alexander (1907) says 'soon after two'; neither is independent. Heth, Hill and Anderson fix the hours around it but give no hour for Lee. A history of 1913 and Long's letter put Lee's sight of the retreat late in the afternoon, which is a later stage. About 14:00 is the best-supported time, from one witness, hedged; weighted, documented.
weighing.who: Pendleton, a brigadier general and chief of artillery, rode near Lee from Cashtown and took position beside him; his report is an official report written by a man who was there. Early (division commander) quotes Pendleton and was himself north of the town. Alexander (artillery colonel with Longstreet) was not present on the afternoon of Jul 1. Heth was on the field and talked to Lee. Long and Taylor were Lee's staff officers, with him. The writer of the 1913 chapter was not there.
weighing.when: Pendleton wrote on 12 Sep 1863, about ten weeks after the day, the nearest writing to the event that gives an hour. Hill (31 Jul) and Anderson (7 Aug 1863) wrote at the same time. Long (1876), Taylor (1877), Heth (1877) and Early (1878) are fourteen to fifteen years after and give no hour for Lee. Alexander (1907) and the history of 1913 are far later, and the Park Service seminar paper of 2018 gives no hour.
weighing.where: Pendleton stood beside Lee 'more than a mile west of the town' on an eminence overlooking the field; this is the first place from which Lee watched the battle, not Seminary Ridge. The 1913 history and Alexander say Seminary Ridge; Pendleton's later sentences (Lee suggested positions on the right to enfilade the valley) show he arrived while the fight was still going and before the line fell back. Reaching Seminary Ridge may therefore be a second stage; the sources do not say.
weighing.how_knew: Pendleton saw Lee arrive and gives the hour with 'perhaps': an estimate, not a clock reading. Heth knew from talking with Lee. Early says he relies on Pendleton. Alexander and the 1913 history give no source.
weighing.clock: Pendleton does not say whose clock he used. The plan notes that the Union and Confederate clocks differed by about 20 minutes (an unsourced estimate) and corrects for neither; the reading here is the Confederate writer's own and is not changed. Hill's 'About 2.30' for Ewell's right wing is a Confederate reading too, so it sits on the same scale as Pendleton's.
weighing.independence: One line of knowledge carries about 14:00 (Pendleton; Early quotes him; Alexander is later and not a witness), so the value is marked single-source. Heth's account that Lee was found while Rodes was heavily engaged, and Hill's about 2.30 for Ewell's wing, are consistent with it and do not state it. No independent witness gives another hour; the values 13:30, 14:30 and 16:30 each rest on a web page, a timeline or a later history.

source_panel_text: About 14:00 on Jul 1: General Pendleton, who rode with Lee, wrote in 1863 that when they took position overlooking the field it was 'perhaps, 2 o'clock'. No writer found gives 13:30 or 14:30; a history of 1913 has Lee on Seminary Ridge about 16:30, a later stage. Three other values are listed.
